data.narrative:
Oxa, a Series D autonomous systems company founded by Paul Newman and Ingmar Posner, operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation exercise draws from a universe of six private peers in the same sector (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, Elroy Air) and no public comparables. Oxa has raised $103M to date.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage peer data points within the narrow Drones & Autonomous category, the peer-median approach was not applicable; the sector contains only five identifiable peers, insufficient to anchor a median valuation. Consequently, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($103M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.5x step-up multiplier typical for Series D advancement yields an implied valuation of $154M.

The triangulated range stands at $131M to $178M, with a central estimate of $154M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 1.5x multiplier for autonomous systems specifically—a sector where capital intensity and commercialization timelines may diverge from broader venture norms—and the lack of granular financial metrics (revenue, burn rate, customer traction) from peer companies. Validation against actual Series D funding terms for comparable autonomous systems companies would meaningfully narrow this band.
